paperTitle: Generating Pixel Art Sprites from Line Art Sketches using Deep Learning
centralContribution: This work demonstrates that state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms can generate pixel art sprites from line art sketches with sufficient quality for direct integration into game products, requiring little to no manual editing by human artists. The study introduces a novel U-Net-based architecture incorporating dense connections, multi-level supervision, and class-weighted focal loss to address the specific challenges of game art generation, which include limited datasets, deviation from natural images, and extreme intolerance to errors.

content.description: Modern game development faces challenges in porting artistic work, with procedural content generation (PCG) seeking automation. Existing image generation techniques are unsuitable for game art due to small datasets, high detail requirements, and intolerance to noise. This paper addresses the scarcity of automatic sprite generation methods by reframing the problem of converting line-art sketches into shaded and colored pixel art as a per-pixel semantic segmentation task, building on previous work's shortcomings with noise and artifacts in coloring.
